passages.t: Gog's defeat and the cleansing of the land
passages.happening:
God will turn Gog around, bring him from the far north to the mountains of Israel, strike the bow from his left hand and the arrows from his right, and he will fall there with all his troops (verses 1-4). ‘So I will make My holy name known among My people Israel’ (verse 7).

Then the people of Israel's cities will go out and burn the weapons, ‘the bucklers and shields, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them for fuel’ (verse 9). God will give Gog a burial place in the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea (verse 11). ‘For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land’ (verse 12), and searchers will mark any bone they find so that it can be buried (verses 14-15). God summons the birds and beasts to a great feast on the mountains of Israel (verses 17-20).
passages.hearers:
The burial place is uncertain. The Sea is probably the Dead Sea, and some connect the name with the mountains of Abarim east of it. Bashan, named in verse 18, was famous for well-fed livestock.

For a priestly writer, the dead left on the land made it unclean, so the long burial is about cleansing the land for God's presence. The weapons burned as fuel picture war itself coming to an end. The feast for birds and beasts is a grim picture drawn from the language of sacrifice, turned on the enemy.
passages.later: Isaiah foresaw swords beaten into plowshares (Isaiah 2:4). The law said that a body left exposed defiled the land (Deuteronomy 21:23).
passages.hard:
Should the seven years of burning weapons and the seven months of burial be taken literally?

Readers who take the Gog oracle as a literal future battle generally read these details literally too. Many other interpreters see the numbers as symbolic, since seven in the Bible commonly signals completeness, and read the pictures as a vivid way of saying that the enemy's defeat is total, that war itself ends, and that the land is thoroughly cleansed. Scholars who read the chapters as early apocalyptic note that the weapons named are simply those of Ezekiel's day, which suggests the prophet is painting in the colors of his own world. The chapter does not settle the question, and faithful Christians differ; this site takes no side. On every reading its message is that God's people will not have to fight the last battle, and that the land will be made clean for his presence. These chapters set no date and identify no modern nation, person or event.
passages.asks: The people of God burned the weapons for years. Ask what weapons you carry, in words or habits, that you could lay down. And ask what peace God might be calling you to make.

passages.happening:
‘I will display My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment that I execute’ (verse 21). ‘From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God’ (verse 22). The nations will know that Israel went into exile for its own sin, and that God hid his face from them (verses 23-24).

‘Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for My holy name’ (verse 25). They will live securely in their land with no one to make them afraid (verse 26). ‘And I will no longer hide My face from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD’ (verse 29).
passages.hearers:
These verses speak directly to the exiles after 587 or 586 BC. The exile had raised the question whether Israel's God had failed. Ezekiel's answer, restated here, is that the exile was God's own judgment on an unfaithful people, and that the restoration will be his act of compassion.

The Gog chapters end not with battle but with the face of God turned toward his people and his Spirit poured out on them, the same promise as the new heart of chapter 36 and the breath in the dry bones of chapter 37.
passages.later: Joel heard the same promise: ‘I will pour out My Spirit on all people’ (Joel 2:28). The priests prayed over Israel that the LORD would ‘cause His face to shine upon you’ (Numbers 6:25).
passages.asks: The chapter ends with God no longer hiding his face. Ask when you have felt that God's face was hidden from you. And ask what it would mean to trust that he will turn toward you again.
